principles: Preserve behavior while changing module shape.
One source of truth for evidence and proof definitions.
New code should have canonical imports; old imports remain compatible.
Do not implement gates or proof authority in a structure-only story.
drivers: Recommended source layout is now documented but not fully present in code.
Flat proof/repro modules have many existing importers, so moving them directly is high blast-radius.
Future Global Control Plane work needs stable runtime/consumption/queue module boundaries.

options.name: A: Compatibility entrypoints first
pros: Build can prove new and legacy paths simultaneously
Creates canonical paths for future work
cons: Implementation remains physically flat behind adapters for now
Requires later migration story to move internals

options.name: B: Move implementations into new directories now
pros: Tree immediately matches the final architecture more literally
cons: Large import churn across proof, repro, gate, and smoke files
Higher risk of breaking lifecycle/proof behavior while trying to do structural cleanup

options.name: C: Only update docs, no code
cons: Does not satisfy the user request to develop the structure
Leaves future hosts without canonical import paths

rationale: Choose compatibility entrypoints first because the user wants development now, but the source tree has many proof/repro importers. This gives future code the recommended paths, keeps existing paths working, and avoids accidentally changing gate/proof behavior.

preMortem.scenario: New directories duplicate proof definitions and drift from flat modules.
preMortem.trigger: A developer copies enums or registries instead of re-exporting existing modules.
preMortem.consequence: Two proof stacks emerge and the architecture goal fails.
preMortem.mitigation: Use re-export adapters only in this slice and add a smoke asserting key symbols are identical across legacy and new paths.

preMortem.scenario: Compatibility shells are mistaken for full migration completion.
preMortem.trigger: Future host sees new folders and assumes implementation has moved.
preMortem.consequence: Follow-up work skips real migration planning.
preMortem.mitigation: Add comments and final notes stating this is milestone 1 compatibility structure, with later migration milestones remaining.

preMortem.scenario: Lifecycle-control skeleton accidentally starts acting as a gate.
preMortem.trigger: Projector types include allow/deny behavior or write lifecycle evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Control Plane becomes a second lifecycle/proof authority.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep skeleton read-only types and no command registration in this story; proof hard-block remains Proof M7.
